issues.description: The proposal hallucinates specific details not found in the Client Matrix, namely '40% growth' and a past client named 'Cascade Freight'. Including fabricated details could severely damage credibility in a competitive bid.
issues.suggested_fix: Remove the references to 40% growth and Cascade Freight. Rely only on the provided background information.

issues.description: The proposal invents specific technologies ('Rails 5', 'Salesforce', 'NetSuite', 'React Native') that are not mentioned in the Client Matrix. The matrix only notes 'Routemaster', a 'driver mobile app', and 'three disconnected systems'.
issues.suggested_fix: Remove the hallucinated technology names and replace them with the generic descriptions provided in the matrix.

issues.description: The proposal misses the Strategic Desired State where the VP of Operations specifically needs a consulting partner to help advocate for incremental improvements internally.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a sentence in the Approach section emphasizing your role as a strategic partner to Operations, helping to build the internal business case for incremental, ROI-driven improvements.

issues.description: Phase 1C dedicates a bullet to ELD compliance workflows, which slightly conflicts with the matrix's goal to make compliance a 'quiet point' and avoid creating new compliance work.
issues.suggested_fix: Reframe the compliance bullet to emphasize that the new workflows will inherently satisfy ELD requirements without requiring a dedicated compliance phase or additional work.

risks: The inclusion of hallucinated facts (growth metrics, specific tech stack, past clients) poses a massive risk to the firm's credibility, especially in a highly competitive engagement with two other firms.
The internal friction between the VP Ops (incremental) and CTO (rebuild) needs careful navigation, as stalling could cause the skeptical CFO to pull funding if Q3 milestones are missed.
